answer: One agent, one pharmacist licence: the national pharmacy board signs the epoch challenge, binding the agent's key to a single licence number re-checked against the public register, and a second key claiming the same licence is refused because the board holds the record. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 licensed pharmacists, each after a four-year degree, exams and registration at roughly $100,000 apiece, about $100,000,000, plus an internship no script can fake. At the summit of trust sits a real credential; its echo is a public register, and a prism of fake licences shatters on one check.
